predecessors.note: 'In 403 BC, the Zhou king formally recognised the existence of the Zhao state along with two other states, Han and Wei.' The Zhao clan had been 'annexing the Baidi state of Dai in the mid-5th century BC'. The Jin dossier carries the matching split.

land.text: Dai (modern Yu County, Hebei), where Prince Jia was proclaimed king in 228

successors.note: Infobox 'Conquered by Qin 222 BC; succeeded by Dai state, Qin state'. Cliopatria's Zhao row ends in 226; the Qin dossier takes Handan in 228 and Dai in 222. The Zhao line restored in 209-205 by Zhao Xie is in the Dai and Chang-shan dossiers of the Eighteen Kingdoms.

capitals.name: Jinyang (Taiyuan)
capitals.note: The Zhao infobox lists Jinyang and Handan; the Handan page calls Handan the second capital 'after Zhongmu' and does not date Zhongmu. The pages give no years for Jinyang.

capitals.name: Handan
capitals.note: 'In 386 BCE, Marquess Jing of Zhao officially relocated the capital to Handan'; 'conquered by the State of Qin after the virtual annexation of Zhao by Qin in 228 BCE'.

capitals.name: Dai (Yu County, Hebei)
capitals.note: Prince Jia 'was proclaimed King Jia at Dai'; the regime 'lasted until 222 BC'. Coordinates are a researcher's reading of Dai County.

rulers.name: Marquess Lie
rulers.note: Reign 409-387 in the text; the infobox gives 403-400 for him. Years follow the infobox, which differs by a year from the text elsewhere (Jing 387-375, Cheng 375-350, Su 350-326, Wuling 326-299, Huiwen 299-266, Xiaocheng 266-245, Daoxiang 245-236, Youmiao 236-228, Jia 228-222).

rulers.name: King Wuling
rulers.note: Abdicated in 299 and died in the Shaqiu Incident in 295.

keyframe_review.note: 57,621 km2 for 404-367 in Shanxi, Hebei and Henan; it holds neither Taiyuan (Jinyang) nor Handan. The infobox gives no area. Cliopatria draws Shangdang (Changzhi) in Zhao from 404, but the Changping page calls it 'Han's Shangdang Commandery' until 262 and Zhao received it only then, so Changzhi is cut out until 262. Jinyang added; years 403-387. Revised 2026-10-19: no Handan disc before 386. The Handan page (re-read) says Jin incorporated Handan in 588 and does not say who held it between 588 and 386; 'In 386 BCE, Marquess Jing of Zhao officially relocated the capital to Handan', Zhao's second capital after Zhongmu. Zhao's shapes are also cut by the wei dossier's Anyi/Hedong and Xihe discs (Cliopatria's Zhao 404 shape reaches Linfen and Changzhi, where Wei's pages put Anyi and Xihe).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 296-263: 'In 296 BC, he annexed the state of Zhongshan' (the Zhao page: 'in 295 BC after a protracted war'). Cliopatria's Zhongshan row ends in 292 and gives its last shape to its 'Wei' row in 291, which this dossier rejects. Revised 2026-10-19: Cliopatria's Zhongshan 292 shape (115.95-117.08 E, 38.57-39.99 N, north-east of Baoding) holds neither Lingshou in Pingshan County, Zhengding nor the Baoding wall that the Zhongshan page names, and the page has Zhao 'surrounding Zhongshan almost entirely' except the north-east. The 296 annexation therefore adds the Zhongshan core (discs at Lingshou, Dongyuan and Baoding; the same discs as the wei dossier's 403-382 Zhongshan) instead of Cliopatria's Zhongshan shape. Cliopatria's 'Wei' shapes from 326 (86,000-97,000 km2 at 112.1-117.2 E, 36.9-40.4 N) contain Dai, Datong, Lingshou and Baoding; I read them as Zhao's northern land and Zhongshan under the wrong label (its 'Zhao' shape sits on Handan, Xingtai, Changzhi and Anyang, its 'Han' 404 shape on Anyi and Luoyang), but only the pages' places are drawn here. The rest of the plain (Dingzhou, Hengshui, Cangzhou) is on no page I opened as Zhao's or anyone's and belongs to no dossier; 381-297 the core is Zhongshan's (independent from 381, 'won its independence back'; the zhongshan dossier is another part's).

notes:
Zhao (趙; Q1574107). Q1574107 is also on Cliopatria's Former Zhao (Han-Zhao, 306-336 CE): a different state, no relation. The Zhao line restored in 209-205 by Zhao Xie (Zhao / Dai of the Eighteen Kingdoms, 'northern Shanxi, northwestern Hebei') is carried by the ea-02 dossiers dai and chang-shan, not by this one; the dossier ends at 222, the Zhao page's end of the Dai regime. Cliopatria's Zhao row is also off the pages: its shapes sit on the Taihang and southern Shanxi and hold neither Taiyuan (Jinyang) nor, before 366, Handan; they hold Changzhi from 404 although Shangdang was Han's until 262; and they include 32 cells of Zheng's last shape. The dossier cuts those and adds discs at Jinyang, Handan, Dai and the northern lands. The row ends in 226 while the pages end the state in 222 (core 228). The Cliopatria 'Wei' row from 326 holds Datong, Baoding and Dingzhou: it is Zhao's north and the Zhongshan plain (see the Wei dossier). Pages opened: Zhao (state), Zhongshan (state), King Wuling of Zhao, Battle of Changping, Handan, King Zhaoxiang of Qin, Qin's wars of unification, Warring States period. Not on any page: when Zhao took Handan from Wei (the Handan page says only that it was relocated to in 386); Zhongmu; the Dai commandery; Great Wall of Zhao; Zhao's border with Yan. The Zhongshan annexation is 305/296 on the Wuling page and 295 on the Zhao page. Gazetteer names wanted: Jinyang, Dai (Yu County), Shangdang, Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, Zhongmu; coordinates used meanwhile.

Revision 2026-10-19 (after review ea-01-d). (1) Zhongshan: Cliopatria's Zhongshan 292 shape is replaced from 296 by the Zhongshan core of the Zhongshan page (discs at Lingshou, Dongyuan, the Baoding wall; 89 cells, the same discs as the wei dossier's 403-382 Zhongshan). The reviewer also named Dingzhou; the Zhongshan page does not mention it, so it is not in the core. 381-297 the core is Zhongshan's own (zhongshan dossier, another part); the rest of the former 'Wei' plain (Hengshui, Cangzhou, Dingzhou, the Xingtai and Handan plain before 386) is on no page I opened and stays with nobody. Cliopatria's 'Wei' 326-224 shapes look like Zhao's northern land and Zhongshan under a wrong label, but I draw only what the pages place. (2) Handan: no Handan disc before 386 (Handan page: Jin from 588, nothing on 588-386); wei and zhao therefore no longer both claim it. (3) Zhao is cut by the wei dossier's Anyi/Hedong and Xihe discs (wei/zhao overlap was 25 cells to 355) and, from 260, by Cliopatria's Later Zhou cells; the 256 gain of Zhou-domain cells (L18) is dropped, those cells being the Qinyang cells Qin took in 265 (Changping page), and eastern-zhou loses to Qin, not Zhao. (4) New events: 376 gain from Jin, 350 gain from and loss to Han (mirrors of han L6/L7, confidence 1). (5) 305 'parts of Zhongshan': a disc at Dongyuan, the page names no place; new keyframe zhao_-305. (6) For the qin owner: qin L39 (222) should name 'zhao', not 'Dai (Prince Jia of Zhao)'. (7) Not done: who held Shangdang after Changping (Zhaoxiang page: 'The combined forces recaptured ... Shangdang', undated); 247 gain of Wey cells has no wey mirror (wey page: nothing on 247).
